title: Drishti: Do Not Forget Slicing While Designing Last-Level Cache Replacement Policies for Many-Core Systems
problem: State-of-the-art LLC replacement policies (Hawkeye, Mockingjay) use a per-slice sampled cache and a per-slice reuse predictor that make myopic decisions based only on accesses to a single slice, unaware of global reuse behavior across all LLC slices in many-core systems; additionally, per-slice sampled cache sets receive insufficient LLC misses to drive accurate replacement decisions.
motivation: Many-core commercial systems universally use sliced LLCs (e.g., 32-64 slices for 32+ cores), but state-of-the-art replacement policies are evaluated and designed for monolithic LLCs, causing their performance advantage to shrink or disappear in sliced configurations.
method: Drishti improves how computer processors decide which data to keep in their largest caches (LLCs), which are split into slices per core. Today's best methods (Hawkeye and Mockingjay) only look within each slice separately, but Drishti adds two fixes: First, each core learns to predict data reuse by watching all its accesses across all slices—getting a complete view without needing extra communication between slices. Second, each slice automatically monitors more cache entries to ensure it sees enough misses to make good decisions. The improvements were tested on systems with 4, 16, and 32 cores, using caches of 8, 32, and 64 MB.
key_novelty: The core contribution is separating the reuse predictor (one per core, looking globally at all its accesses) from the cache monitoring (local to each slice), so policies can infer global reuse patterns without adding extra messages between slices.
contributions: Analysis identifying that state-of-the-art LLC replacement policies lose effectiveness in many-core sliced LLC configurations due to myopic per-slice prediction and under-sampled sets
Per-core global reuse predictor combined with per-slice local sampled cache, eliminating centralized interconnect traffic while capturing global reuse patterns
Per-slice dynamic sampled cache improving LLC miss coverage per slice
On a 32-core system: Mockingjay improved from 6.7% to 13.2% over LRU; Hawkeye improved from 3.3% to 5.6% over LRU

metrics.speedup: 5.6% IPC improvement (Hawkeye+Drishti) and 13.2% (Mockingjay+Drishti) over LRU on 32-core system
metrics.other: Without Drishti: Hawkeye 3.3%, Mockingjay 6.7% over LRU; Drishti roughly doubles the gain

primary_theme: sliced-LLC-aware last-level cache replacement policy design
